text:
sarah_sales: Quick heads-up: NimbusSoft wants a performance proof for their gen-chat workflow. Goal: sustained 600 QPS, client p50 <120ms, p99 <500ms, median payload ~5k tokens. Ask: 1) load plan for adaptive stress, 2) a one-paragraph external-friendly summary, 3) hosted vs dedicated hour/day cost sketch, 4) short KMS/HSM & SOC2 bullets we can paste into their security questionnaire. Can infra/SRE take the lead? POC ref: NIM-POC-42

raj_infra: We'll own the run. Proposed plan: ramp to 600 in 4m, hold 45m, and schedule jittered microbursts (50reqs x 8s every 90s) to exercise scheduler and tails. Use quantized 13B variant with prefix KV cache on. Need confirmation they accept Redwood-quantized model (not customer weights).

sarah_sales: They confirmed: RHF-finetuned 13B, ok to use our quantized build. They also called out KMS integration and a few SOC2 evidence items.

maya_vm: Security quick notes: Dedicated/Private support customer-managed KMS key wrapping (we can provide key ARN examples). HSM available through partner integration with additional SOW. Audit logs: export to customer's SIEM via syslog/Kinesis. SOC2: we can provide cert copy and scoped artifacts for infra controls. I'll draft text for the questionnaire.

deploy-bot: Deployment to nimbus-stg-3 completed at 1790011200 :rocket:

leo_sre: Runbook (sketch):
- cluster: nimbus-stg-3
- model: rhf-13b-q (quantized)
- command:
  ./stress_run --target 600 --ramp 240 --hold 2700 --microburst "50x8s@90s-jitter" --model rhf-13b-q --prefix_cache=on --trace=sample
- collect: p50/p95/p99, token/sec, GPU util, KV hit %, GC/driver logs
- warm: seed prefixes for first 20m to simulate steady traffic
- alerts: p50>220ms or p99>900ms -> scale and pause new traffic

raj_infra: Running now. Will post summary + S3 artifacts.

raj_infra: RUN SUMMARY:
- sustained target: 600 QPS held for 45m
- avg payload observed: 5.05k tokens
- token throughput: ~13.6M tokens/hr
- client latencies: p50=105ms, p95=312ms, p99=495ms
- microburst tails: brief p99 spikes up to ~760ms during bursts
- GPU util: 68% avg
- KV cache hit rate: 41% (high prefix diversity)
- errors: 0.02% transient retries during two microburst windows
- notes: one node showed elevated scheduling latency correlated with a kernel driver retry; auto-recoverd. No OOMs.

raj_infra: Artifacts: s3://redwood-artifacts/nimbus-poc/1790012000/{metrics.csv,traces.zip,config.json}

sarah_sales: Great. Can you give a crisp hosted vs dedicated cost sketch and a 1-paragraph blurb we can send? Keep public-safe language.

raj_infra: Cost sketch (ballpark): Hosted inference list ~ $0.33 / 1k tokens. At 13.6M tokens/hr => ~$4,488/hr. Dedicated/reserved equivalent infra estimate: ~$950-1,050/hr depending on instance family and commit term. 30d sustained reserved can lower unit cost ~35-45%.

raj_infra: Shareable blurb:
"We executed an adaptive stress run for NimbusSoft's 13B workflow and validated sustained 600 QPS for 45 minutes with client-observed p50 ≈105ms and p99 ≈495ms. Microbursts produced short tail spikes (~760ms) but no OOMs or service crashes. Estimated hosted inference is ≈$4.5k/hr at this throughput; Dedicated reserved capacity can reduce the hourly equivalent to roughly $950–$1,050 depending on commit. We recommend modest prefix warming and KV cache tuning to reduce tail latency further."

omar_sales_ops: For proposal: suggest a 3-day pilot with a 30% pilot credit on hosted usage, or a 1-month trial of reserved capacity at 50% list for onboarding. I'll prepare options once artifacts are finalized.

maya_vm: I uploaded a draft security response set to the questionnaire ticket and invited Nimbus security for Tue 10am PT meeting.

sarah_sales: Thanks team — I'll send the blurb and artifacts, and confirm the security call. Raj/Leo: follow up on the node scheduling noise and see if a kernel driver patch or node replacement is needed.

leo_sre: Will investigate and report back. Good run overall.

sarah_sales: ✅ closing loop. Thanks all :tada:
